description: `if x && x > 1` -- narrowing that has to flow out of a **compound condition**. `&&` desugars to a temp plus a nested if, so the outer if's condition position holds an entire `seq`, and the then-branch uses `x` rather than the temp. Two things follow: the checker cannot read the tested variable off the condition's syntax, and the refinement established inside the condition has to survive being carried out of it. Note also that `x > 1` inside the condition already needs x narrowed -- the refinement is used in the same expression that establishes it.
